t: Is Array a Preorder of Some Binary Tree — Stack of Open Nodes
o: We get nodes in the claimed preorder order along with parent ids, and must verify consistency. In a preorder traversal, each node's children appear immediately after it: first the whole left subtree, then the right child. So when a node appears, its parent must be the MOST RECENT node that still has an unfilled child slot. Maintain a stack of (id, remainingSlots=2). Example 2 fails because after visiting 1 (which still expects a child), node 2 claims parent 0, which is buried under 1 on the stack.
k: A preorder sequence is valid iff every node's parent is the top of a stack of nodes with open child slots.

a.i: Push each visited node with 2 slots. When the next node arrives, its parent must equal the stack top; otherwise the previous subtree boundary was violated. Decrement the parent's slot count and pop it when both children are placed.
s: First node must have parentId == -1; push it with 2 slots.
For each following node: stack must be non-empty and top's id must equal its parentId, else return false.
Decrement top's slots; pop while top has 0 slots; push the new node with 2 slots.
Return true after processing all nodes.

a.n: Recursive Descent with Parent Index Map
a.i: Map each id to its position. Recursively verify: starting at position 0 (must be the root), a segment [lo,hi) is a valid preorder block for a subtree rooted at nodes[lo] if its children's blocks tile the remainder contiguously, each child's parent being nodes[lo]'s id.
s: Build id→index map; check root is first with parent -1.
Recursively consume positions: after the root, parse up to two contiguous child blocks whose parents equal the root id.
Succeed iff the recursion consumes exactly all nodes.
a.t: O(n) — each position consumed once (recursion depth may be O(n))

w: The stack approach is preferred (iterative, no deep recursion). Pitfall: forgetting the root-parent check, or allowing a node's parent to be anywhere in the stack rather than strictly the top.
